speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Nothing would make me consider having one more child." The Government has tried many financial incentives, but what we need is something money cannot buy – time.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Over the weekend, I visited residents and one had a doormat which read "Tired Adults Club".

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I jokingly said that I am from the same club.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think many of us here are also from the same club.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But the more I thought about it, the less funny it seemed.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Young Singaporeans have little breathing space to socialise, to build a community, to find life partners.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Young couples try the Build-To-Order (BTO) again and again to no avail.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mothers are regarded as risky hires because maternity leave is seen by some employers as a problem to be managed, rather than a milestone to be supported.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Infant care waitlists are measured in months, not weeks, and children are too often tolerated rather treasured, seen as noise in public places, inconveniences to career progression and financial burdens rather than the precious gift they are.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We have built world-class infrastructure for economic productivity and ingrained in ourselves a hardworking work culture.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But we may not have built the equivalent infrastructure, nor inculcated the same priorities for family life.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We must question whether a successful career and a successful home are mutually exclusive.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We need a fundamental rethink across four pillars: time, care, work and housing.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first pillar is time and breathing space.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We cannot build strong families if our young people and parents are running on empty and feel they do not have space to breathe.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Work can be all consuming if left to our own devices.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We need to provide for employers to be able to play their part.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Seven days of annual leave is really too short.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Let us structurally mandate breathing space for our young people to socialise and date, and for people to spend quality time with their families.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We need to structurally mandate "breathing space" for our young people to socialise and date, and for people to spend quality time with their families.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Children frequently require checkups and may experience extended bouts of illness.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Childcare leave is currently only six days for those aged 0-7, and many times, these are just sufficient to cover preschool closure days.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Childcare leave drops to two days for those aged 8-12.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If just one child catches hand, foot and mouth disease, how will families cope?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On this, I note that my fellow Members David Hoe and Charlene Chen had raised related Parliamentary Questions last year and they were told that the Government is committed to supporting working parents in caring for heir children and that the Ministry will be reviewing the leave provisions.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) to give an update on the review of the leave policies?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second pillar is strengthening the structures of care.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To care for children well, childcare must make sense.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We therefore need to relook our policies on childcare, childminding, postpartum care and transport-related friction for care journeys.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, childcare subsidies should be the same for everyone.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Non-working mothers receive significantly less subsidy than working mothers.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This penalises mothers who choose to be stay-at-home caregivers to their second or subsequent newborn children, or those with modern work arrangements.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For example, a mother working as a freelancer may not accumulate enough formal hours to qualify for the working mother subsidy.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Childcare is an essential form of early childhood education and care.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Such basic subsidies should be universal for all children, regardless of the mother's employment status.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As a mother shared with me at a People's Action Party Women's Wing Listening Session two weeks ago: "Why s unpaid caregiving at home less valuable than the contributions of a working mom?" Second, we must increase the accessibility of childcare centres.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There are parts of Singapore where parents face long waitlists for nearby Ministry of Education Kindergartens (MK), anchor-operator (AOP) or partner-operator (POP) childcare centres.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On the other hand, some centres in older neighbourhoods may have lower take-up.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To address this spatial mismatch, we could provide a limited subsidy to such underutilised operators to fund shuttle services, regardless of whether they are MK, AOP or POP, much like the school bus system our primary school children enjoy.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This helps reduce geographic friction, improves spatial mobility and achieves better allocative efficiency for childcare services.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I also propose that, beyond AOP and POP, the Government extends site tender access to all operators, including mid-tier operators, to scale centres to neighbourhoods with high demand.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This helps alleviate the high demand with a higher and more diverse supply of options for parents, and not only the Government-supported centres.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Third, we must scale and improve access to flexible childminding options.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Families with children often need extra caregiver help.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If there is no grandparent or domestic help, parents need additional childminding options.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are there plans to expand the pilot or increase publicity for the pilot?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And will the pilot be made permanent and scaled up?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If so, what is the timeline for that?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In addition to such professional childminding services, I hope to see neighbourly childminding normalised in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In Bishan, some playground mummies organise playdates and take turns to look after one another's children.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How can we facilitate more of these and build a stronger communal parenting culture?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As families in the same estate become friends, they may feel more assured in leaving their children to be minded by one another's families when needs or extenuating circumstances arise.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We can suggest guidelines for the respective families to adopt in such informal childminding in the neighbourhood.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If new parents are well supported in this regard, they will feel more confident in subsequently having more children.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As I have previously raised in this House, I propose comprehensive home visitation postpartum support.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While we currently have follow-up healthcare after delivery, we should enhance this with structured in-home postpartum visits in the first year.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Trained maternity nurses could provide guidance on newborn care, breastfeeding, physiotherapy and mental health screening.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They could also identify signs of family stress, social isolation or financial difficulty, and coordinate follow-up support with health and social services so families can receive timely counselling and financial assistance.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In all of this, we should not overlook fathers.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Yet, fathers often feel like bystanders, unsure how to help and anxious about a wife recovering from birth and a baby they do not yet know how to hold.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If postpartum support is to strengthen the whole family, it must include fathers too.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I therefore propose that the structured in-home postpartum visits deliberately engage fathers, offering practical guidance on newborn care, on supporting a spouse's physical and emotional recovery, and on recognising the signs of postnatal depression in their spouses, and in themselves.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Let us equip fathers to be confident co-parents rather than well-meaning "helpers", so we can build the equal parenting that I hope will one day be the norm in every Singaporean family.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Fifth, to reduce transport-related friction for care journeys, I propose a transport care credit scheme.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is a targeted, flexible transport support for low to lower-middle-income families in Singapore who face high "care journey" transport costs due to family members with specific needs – young children, elderly, persons with permanent or temporary disabilities or medical conditions, where use of public transport is impractical, insufficient, challenging, or burdensome. "Care journeys" would be trips to hospitals, polyclinics or therapy centres.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The grant will be in the form of credits, which can be used for a range of transport options, such as public transport fares, taxis, private hire vehicles and car sharing.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The proposed grant will address the "last mile" problem for individuals and caregivers who need non-standard public transport options for themselves or frail or young dependents but do not qualify for existing disability-specific work schemes.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I note that my fellow Member David Hoe had raised a related Parliamentary Question in February.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the PMO also be able to give an update on the review of these policies?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The third pillar is empowering women and protecting careers.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Women who have children in Singapore experience reductions in earnings and career advancement.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, hiring maternity cover for a brief 16 weeks is incredibly difficult for employers.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: By the time they can find the right person and train them, time is over.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, mothers feel pressured to rush back to work at the end of the 16 weeks when they may not be ready, in order to keep their jobs.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They may end up returning to work but utilising other types of leave or means to provide stepped-down caregiving to their newborn.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A six to 12-month window makes it viable for employers to hire contract cover, removing the pressure on mothers to rush back and allowing employers to retain them long-term.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Small employers may face cashflow issues as the Government payment of maternity and other related leave will only be paid on a reimbursement basis, even while the employers may hire additional maternity covers.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the Government consider a mechanism that could alleviate such cashflow issues for employers?

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, I propose we introduce a Career Comeback Tax Credit for employers who hire returning stay-at-home parents.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Additionally, we should also encourage employers to redesign certain jobs to offer part-time roles for parents of young children, allowing companies to augment their workforce while keeping parents engaged in the economy so that it will not be a binary choice only between full-time parenting or full-time employment.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Third, we should incentivise and encourage employers to provide flexibility in work schedules and private spaces for mothers to pump breast milk at work.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I suggest we introduce a "Make It Work" grant for building owners to install self-contained, lockable lactation pods to provide a safe and conducive space for working moms to pump breast milk at work, and it could include refrigerator space to store breast milk.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should, of course, caution the public against the potential misperception that EEF would work miracles.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Even as we make EEF more accessible, we should also mitigate the potential issue that subsidising EEF might inadvertently encourage couples to intentionally delay marriage and parenthood.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, EEF is increasingly becoming a necessary response to the reality of later marriages, where our fertility will be adversely affected.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: While take-up rates might be modest initially, preserving fertility offers couples a vital option.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Once the biological clock passes, it is past.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should give couples the chance of still having children.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The fourth pillar is housing for family formation.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Our housing policies must proactively encourage larger and inter-generational families.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should mandate that HDB designs future blocks to make this practically feasible.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Additionally, families with two or more young children should be given priority and expanded options to ballot and receive additional grants for 5-room or larger units across BTO and Sales of Balance Flats.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Currently, there is a Third Child Priority Scheme.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should have a "Second Child Priority Scheme" also for 5-room BTOs and Sales of Balance Flats.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If a family has a second or subsequent child and needs to upgrade to a 5-room flat, they can receive a targeted CPF grant to offset the cost of a larger resale flat.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This solves the spatial issue now, without waiting for BTO construction.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am asking the Government to make a wholly different and wholesome kind of commitment, so people feel secure raising a family in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Even so, the Government alone cannot solve this.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So that our society will view parenthood as valuable, beautiful, joyful and not a high stakes competition, so that everyone will play their part in supporting families to flourish.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And as a stay-at-home father told me, so that success in Singapore can go beyond the "5Cs", but also celebrate our children, the “C” that matters the most for building our nation.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some people have told me they do not want to bring children into a world of pain and suffering.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But there is also much joy and beauty that our world still holds.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Very often, I see that in the eyes of a young child.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: When I see our children, I see the future of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Joyful, energetic, caring and most precious of all, cute.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Like many others, I was delighted when we saw selfies of babies popping up on the official LTA, MCCY, and gov.sg's social media pages.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And many of us felt a spark of that childlike wonder and joy.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That is the kind of Singapore I hope we will build.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Not a tired adults club but a country that actually has the time and space to enjoy our children.

speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And in that Singapore, if we were to ask couples if they want to have one more child, the answer would be, "Why not?"

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Indeed, many of her observations are consistent with feedback that we have received regarding marriage and parenthood.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Since the Workgroup was announced, many Singaporeans have come forward to share their suggestions and lived experiences, and we have also conducted many engagements.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Across these conversations, what is clear is that Singaporeans do value family, relationships and meaningful connections.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, they also encounter challenges and practical realities in pursuit of their marriage and parenthood aspirations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Recently released statistics on marriage and parenthood have also sharpened our urgency to act.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, the Workgroup’s focus is to see how we can better support Singaporeans across the whole marriage and parenthood journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To that end, we are developing a long-term roadmap to strengthen support for marriage and parenthood, mobilise whole-of-society action and support a broader societal reset.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Chen has insightfully identified some of the key issues that influence M&P decisions, which are time, care, work and housing.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Chen called for more leave days to address the scarcity of time and the challenges faced by parents in managing work and caregiving commitments.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are actively working on how we can provide more protected time for working parents while managing the impact on business operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Workplace culture and norms have a strong impact on how well-supported parents feel at work and whether they are able to utilise their statutory leave provisions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Line managers and supervisors, in particular, can make all the difference as they are the ones who approve such leave.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: How they do so and whether well-managed covering arrangements are in place can make a big difference.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While many associate FWAs with working from home, it is also much broader than that.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A recent CNA article found that flexi-time and flexi-load may matter much more for parents, as it gives them the space to manage their work schedules in ways that best meet their responsibilities at work and at home.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will continue to push for these flexible arrangements to support parents better.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To Ms Chen's point on job redesign and part-time work, employers can tap on the Productivity Solutions Grant to offset the costs of adopting FWAs and the SkillsFuture Workforce Development Grant (Job Redesign+) to engage consultancy services to support enterprise job redesign.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They can also benefit from FWA implementation resources and training by tripartite partners and the Institute of Human Resource Professionals to better implement work-life friendly practices.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Chen also highlighted the challenges parents face in returning to work after parental leave or after taking a temporary career break to focus on caring for their children.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We agree that this is an important area that needs to be tackled.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have been enhancing measures to support career transitions, employment facilitation and reskilling.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Examples include, the Skills and Workforce Development Agency's (SWDA's) HerCareer initiative for women jobseekers and career advisory and skills training offered by SWDA and the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) Employment and Employability Institute (e2i).

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Jobseekers can also tap on Career Conversion Programmes and the Mid-Career Pathways Programme to improve their employability and be placed in a new role.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are exploring how we can better support returning parents beyond these current initiatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Employers can also support parents by providing family-friendly infrastructure and amenities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, they can support breastfeeding mothers by tapping on NTUC's Better Workplace Programmes to set up proper lactation spaces or the Building and Construction Authority's (BCA's) Accessibility Fund to retrofit their premises with universal design features, including lactation facilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On housing, we agree with Ms Chen that housing is an important determinant in marriage and parenthood.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We currently provide larger families a range of housing options to meet their need for more space.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, multi-generation families may apply for 3Gen flats, which are specifically designed for extended families who wish to live under one roof.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Flat owners may also apply to combine two adjoining 3-room or smaller flats under the Conversion of Adjoining Flats Scheme.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also recently enhanced the Third Child Priority Scheme, which gives priority in BTO and SBF exercises to eligible families with three or more children.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are exploring what more we can do and we will study Ms Chen's suggestions as part of the Workgroup.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, women can already receive Government subsidies and tap on MediSave for egg freezing done on medical grounds, for example, to preserve fertility before undergoing cancer treatment.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will also study her suggestions on postpartum support.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ms Chen also highlighted the importance of enhancing care infrastructure.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have also enhanced preschool affordability for all.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Applicants who are not working due to extenuating circumstances and need full-day childcare can apply for special approval to receive subsidy support equivalent to what a working applicant can receive.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will do more to support parents in caregiving and will take Ms Chen's suggestions into account.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On Early Childhood Development Agency's (ECDA's) infant childminding pilot, feedback from parents and childminders so far has been positive.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will review the learnings from the pilot in considering additional moves and will bear Ms Chen's suggestions in mind.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Over and above policy moves, support for marriage and parenthood must be a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Workgroup is looking at how we can bring on board all segments of society to participate in this.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I am heartened that various groups will put forth their suggestions to the Workgroup, such as the joint White Paper on fertility and human development by National University of Singapore Medicine and the Population Association of Singapore, and the People's Action Party Women's Wing.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the coming months, we will continue to engage widely across society, with Singaporeans, businesses and community partners.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We invite all Singaporeans to be part of this Reset – to contribute their ideas, lend their support and help shape a Singapore where families are not only supported, but can truly flourish.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If it was 14 years, it would be mind-boggling.
